chapter: Small's Paradise, Fletcher Henderson and Horace
title: Elmer Snowden's band at Small's, and Garvin Bushell's many instruments
summary: Snowden picked good players; Garvin Bushell, first seen in Chicago with Lucille Hegamin, played oboe, flute and bassoon and the band played overture excerpts at intermission.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Then it says here that you worked with Elmer Snowden again. This was in Small's?
Small's.
And this is when the band is really good, isn't it?

Yeah. He had a very good (unintelligible) picking musicians and got the band he wanted. And Cliff was very nice too about it. Well, them fellows, you know, they brought up in (unintelligible) from the old school coming up, the old fellows would --
Well, then it was -- almost always he had Garvin Bushell in the band.
Garvin's a fine musician, Garvin Bushell. First time I saw Garvin Bushell, he came to Chicago with Lucille Hegamin.
The blues singer.
Right. And we were just running around Chicago playing clarinet then when he came there with Lucille Hegamin.
Well, Elmer, I think, told me that he played oboe or something.
Oboe, flute, clarinet, saxophone, bassoon, good musician.
Well, what -- what sort of numbers was he using these instruments on?
When he was with Lucille, clarinet and --
I mean with Elmer.
What I was using?
I mean what did Elmer -- what sort of numbers did you use these instruments on?
Well, he --
With Elmer Snowden --

Well, at that time we'd be playing in like the Nest Club or some other club, and they'd have a lot of excerpts from the big overtures, which (unintelligible) which was, you know, and broke them down and fit for a seven piece, eight piece group, and clarinet was included in it, parts clarinet, and sometimes you substitute (unintelligible) sopranos for the clarinet, but that's the way it was, called excerpts from overtures (unintelligible).
I mean would they be a part of the show?
No, that was for the intermission. Then we go on intermission, and piano player probably would stay back there and play for the entertainers, and we'd take
our hour's intermission off, go or out down.
But I mean if Garvin was going to play oboe or bassoon or something, I mean what would that be, like a fake oriental number or --

Well, mostly like an oriental number, but he didn't play it that much. Then after we started working with the different groups, bigger bands, these were very well finished fitted musicians, and he would -- then he'd go back and he'd take a flute. He had his bassoon, oboe, could already play the clarinet and saxophone. Of course, the of all woodwind instruments clarinet is the master bassoon (unintelligible), but it's -- and it's, you know, you have three octaves on the clarinet, came out low register and you can knock that little (unintelligible) up in the middle register changing keys.
